source_metadata.title: Quipu: A Governed Bitemporal Knowledge Graph Store
source_metadata.subtitle: Start strict: rethinking knowledge-graph defaults for agent-written knowledge
source_metadata.design: AI/ML systems and software architecture study with a deterministic seeded benchmark, a small agent arm, a real governed-writer trace, and an external evidence-sufficiency benchmark

source_consistency_findings: The paper header prints August 18, 2026, while the arXiv version marker identifies v1 as 17 Aug 2026. The output uses the arXiv submission date for version identity and preserves the PDF header date in the SEA metadata note.

The SARC comparison agrees on verdict, placement, and response but differs on coverage semantics for the faithful export. The padded export removes those discrepancies; the outputs do not collapse these two export conditions.

The DEMM evaluation is described as external because it uses DEMM-Bench contracts and construction oracle, but Quipu was self-added as a ninth regime and the adapter and reader are study-authored. The appraisal treats this as partial external anchoring rather than independent external validation.
extraction_limitations: Atoms are grounded in arXiv:2608.16813v1 and remain marked needs_review pending human verification.

The quantitative schema is clinically oriented. Benchmark units such as writes, probes, decisions, and property judgments are represented as population, exposure, and outcome context only where the mapping is direct and source-supported.
Single-run latency figures and prototype query timings are preserved as engineering characterization, not comparative performance evidence.
Repeated textual restatements were not duplicated as atoms. The set favors independently reviewable design rules, methods, benchmark results, limitations, disclosures, and conclusions.
schema_gaps: The current LiteratureAtom schema has no dedicated software-architecture principle, benchmark-configuration, reproducibility, governance-evidence, or implementation-performance atom kinds. These assertions use method, quantitative_result, qualitative_result, limitation, other, and author_conclusion without changing the schema.
